plain_english_policy: This bill provides a temporary transition period for economic development projects that were already in the planning stages before new wage rules took effect. Specifically, it allows companies to apply for tax incentives under the old base wage requirements if they submitted their intent to invest on or before November 21, 2009. The official text states: 'The Legislature desires to have a transition period for the approval of certain projects based on certain requirements under existing law before the effective date of Act 2009-722.' Consequently, any qualifying project with an application filed by that deadline will be judged against the pre-existing wage standards rather than the stricter new ones introduced in Act 2009-722.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would preserve eligibility for tax incentives under previous (lower) base wage requirements for specific economic development projects, provided their written statement of intent was filed with the Department of Revenue on or before November 21, 2009. This effectively delays the application of new higher wage mandates to these legacy applications.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives Knight, Fields and Oden advanced this bill.
evidence_quotes: "The Legislature desires to have a transition period for the approval of certain projects based on certain requirements under existing law before the effective date of Act 2009-722."

"for the purposes of any qualifying project... filed a written statement of intent... with the Department of Revenue on or before November 21, 2009, the term 'base wage requirement' as defined in Section 40-18-190(a)(1)a. means the term 'base wage requirement' as defined in Section 40-18-190(a)(1) prior to the effective date of Act 2009-722."
